title: The Nyaya Sutras, with Vatsyayana's Bhashya
author: gautama
attributionNote: The sutras are ascribed to Gautama, also called Akshapada, and were given their received form over several centuries. The Bhashya beside them is the work of Vatsyayana, also called Pakshilasvamin, and is the base text of the whole later Nyaya literature.
description: The Nyaya Sutras set out the means by which anything is known at all — perception, inference, comparison and testimony — and then the objects to be known, the body, the senses, the self and its liberation. They define debate itself: what counts as a reason, where an argument goes wrong, how a question is answered, what makes a rejoinder a mere quibble. Vatsyayana's Bhashya works through each aphorism with examples drawn from daily life and from the schools he refutes.
historicalContext: With the Vaisheshika school the Nyaya formed the analytical wing of Indian philosophy, and in the Navya-Nyaya of later Bengal its logic was carried further than any other Indian school. The Bhashya is the oldest commentary that survives and the standard of correctness for all that followed.
availabilityNote: Complete: all five adhyayas with their ahnikas and 529 units of the GRETIL e-text, streamed at read time one ahnika at a time. The sutras and Vatsyayana's Bhashya are read from the same GRETIL file under their own reference markers and shown in separate panes; the file is a plain transcription and has not been proof-read by the inputter.
